entries.title: Roofs that differ like a real town's
entries.summary: House roofs are no longer all the same gable: they're pitched differently, about a third are hipped (pyramids over square houses), and some are mended with a tarp, holed, or have a skylight.
entries.body:
- **Pitch**: roofs rise anywhere from shallow to steep instead of all at one angle.
- **Hipped roofs**: about a third slope down on all four sides, with tiles over the hips and gutters all round; over a square house they make a pyramid.
- **Mending and damage**: here and there a roof has a tarpaulin pulled over it, heaped over the broken tiles and creased where old tyres and a sandbag weigh it down, its corners tied to the gutter; or a hole with the battens showing.
- **Skylights** are let into some roofs, and a few of them are lit after dark.
- **Lamplight after dark** is softer: a lit window or skylight gleams instead of flaring.
- **Lamps go out** in a ruined house, and in a house once it's shelled, loses a wall or its roof catches fire.
- Chimneys sit properly on whatever slope is under them. Roofs are still scenery only, so cover and movement are unchanged.

screenshots.caption: Four houses from the street, from behind and after dark, a tarp close up, a ruin after dark, and the town from above, before and after

entries.title: Rubble that looks like rubble
entries.summary: Where a wall has come down, the rubble is a heap of broken masonry with bricks, plaster slabs, a charred joist and bent rods sticking out, instead of grey blocks.
entries.body:
- **A heap, not blocks**: rubble is a rough mound of broken masonry, highest to one side.
- **On it**: lumps of brick (some still mortared together), slabs of painted plaster, a joist or two run up out of it, charred or bare, and reinforcing rods bent out of the concrete.
- It gives the same cover as before, whether the map put it there or a wall was just brought down.

screenshots.caption: Rubble heaps and a ruined house, before and after

entries.title: Shop fronts on the town's main streets
entries.summary: The shops by the town square look like shops: a painted fascia with the shop's name, a striped awning, a hanging sign, and their wares out on the pavement.
entries.body:
- **Fascias**: each shop has a painted board over its windows with its name in raised letters, and about half have a sign standing out from the wall on a bracket.
- **Awnings**: striped canvas on metal arms with a scalloped edge, in the shop's colours, high enough to walk under.
- **On the pavement**, clear of the door: a **greengrocer's** crates of fruit and vegetables on a stand, a **cafe's** tables and chairs, a **baker's** sandwich board and tubs of flowers, a **hardware shop's** sacks, gas bottles and buckets, a **newsagent's** paper rack and board.
- The wares are scenery: no cover, and a shell or a passing truck knocks them over.

screenshots.caption: A parade of shops and a shop in town, before and after

entries.title: No more stutter when parked cars and wrecks come into view
entries.summary: Panning across a town froze the picture for a tenth to a quarter of a second each time a parked car or a burnt-out tank came into view. Now a car is put together over a few frames, and wrecks and cars that look alike are copied.
entries.body:
- A car coming into view costs at most a few hundredths of a second spread over a few frames, where it used to cost 100-290 ms in one. It appears a fraction of a second later instead.
- Burnt-out tanks are all the same hulk, so every one after the first is copied in about 5 ms instead of built in about 190. Cars of the same model and paint are copied the same way.
- Battles load a little faster too: the map's hulks used to take nearly two seconds of the load.
- Cars and wrecks look exactly as before.

entries.title: Smoother frame rate over towns, fewer stutters
entries.summary: Looking over the town draws about a third as much as before, so the frame rate there roughly doubles, and panning or jumping the camera seldom stalls while scenery and grass are built.
entries.body:
- **Towns draw far less.** Houses, garden walls and trees are merged block by block as soon as a block is built (in a town that used to wait for the whole neighbourhood, so it hardly ever happened), and each model casts its shadow from one shape instead of one per material. Over the town, the draws a frame fell from about 8,000 to about 2,000, and the time the processor spends preparing the picture from 17 ms to under 6.
- **Far fewer freezes on camera moves.** Scenery and grass coming into view are built nearest first, a few milliseconds' worth each frame, instead of all in one frame (up to most of a second over a street of houses). A parked car or wreck seen for the first time still costs a short hitch.
- **Vehicles appear faster.** Their distant-view meshes are made once for each kind and shared, so a tank's model builds in about a third of the time.
- **Solo battles' connection readout** (in the console's `why` and `net`) now says that the host is your own computer and its round trip follows your frame rate, instead of blaming the network.

screenshots.caption: The same town views before and after: the picture is unchanged, drawn in well under half the draws

entries.title: Town streets that look lived in
entries.summary: Town roads, sidewalks and the square look like real, used streets now: worn asphalt with patched repairs and sealed cracks, drain grates and manholes, faded markings, and paving laid slab by slab.
entries.body:
- **Asphalt** wears the way traffic wears it: tyres polish the wheel paths, oil drips down the middle of each lane, and grit and damp gather in the gutters along the kerb.
- **Repairs** show as saw-cut patches of newer asphalt edged with sealant, instead of flat black boxes, and cracks are filled with tar.
- **Drain grates** sit in the gutters and **manhole covers** in the lanes.
- **Zebra crossings and parking bays** are painted on the road, so they pick up its grain and wear through in places. The centre line stops short of each crossing.
- **Sidewalks** shade each slab along its real joints, not a grid laid across them, and lose the pink cast. The odd slab has been relaid or stained.
- **The square** is paved in large stone slabs instead of a pink checkerboard of tiles.
- **Kerbs** are a quieter grey instead of a bright white strip.
- **In the rain** the junctions, crossings and car parks get as wet as the road round them.

screenshots.caption: The town's central crossroads and square from the same cameras, before and after

entries.title: A steadier step across trench edges
entries.summary: Soldiers use separate takeoff and landing poses as they cross a trench lip. Close up, Rebel fighters and their medics use the animated infantry model with faction colors and their own equipment.
entries.body: The existing clip preserves the original framing and playback speed. Foliage partly hides foot placement, and the dark character view does not establish close-up animation or equipment quality.

videos.caption: Same cameras and seed. The first pair compares the previous trench fix with the directional animation. The second pair compares the original and skinned infantry. Watch the soldier beside the vehicle step into the trench, then compare the Rebel fighters and medic.

entries.title: Better-built decks, truck bodies, launchers, lamps and aircraft stores
entries.summary: Twenty more vehicle parts now share one detailed design across the roster: engine grilles, track running gear, truck beds and box bodies, missile launchers, lamps, gun mounts, missiles, pods and engine intakes.
entries.body:
- Engine decks, radiators and exhausts have recessed grilles with proper slats; tank tracks have rubber-tyred
  return rollers and hinged, raked skirt panels; smoke dischargers sit on bolted brackets with their firing
  cables.
- Truck beds have rails, stake posts, hinged dropsides and tailgates. Workshop and medical bodies have framed
  doors, roller shutters and ladders. Pickup gun mounts stand on braced posts behind proper shields, with
  welded roll cages and bull bars.
- Missile launch boxes show their tube mouths. Lamps sit in housings with guards and indicators.
- Missiles have real noses, seekers and thin fins, and pods carry their lugs and seams. The A-10's engine fans
  are finally visible in its intakes, and helicopters gain detailed hub caps, pylons and sensor mounts.
- The T-55's splash board and the BTR-80's window frames, which were hidden inside the hull, now show.
- Every gun still fires from exactly the same point.

screenshots.caption: Matched close-ups: before on the left, after on the right. The A-10's engine fan, the T-55's glacis, the Bradley's TOW launcher, HEMTT and Zamak repair bodies, the Humvee's front, an offroad gun mount and an F-16's underwing stores.

entries.title: Better-built running gear, crew fittings, cranes and aircraft details
entries.summary: Forty more vehicle parts now share one detailed design: track guards, tow cables, suspension, exhausts, searchlights, light bars, benches, tanker walkways, cranes, gun mounts, muzzle brakes, aircraft landing gear, bombs and more.
entries.body:
- Tanks have bolted track guards with brackets and hinged mudguards, spare track links on retaining bars,
  stowed tow cables with thimble eyes, muzzle brakes, muzzle sensors and proper pintle mounts for their
  machine guns. Self-propelled guns rest on travel locks and recoil on real hydraulic cylinders.
- Wheeled vehicles have suspension arms with coil-over dampers, routed exhausts with silencers, air-cleaner
  stacks, searchlights, light bars and beacons, number plates, and lever handles on armoured doors.
- Trucks gain benches, tanker walkways with manholes and handrails, pump cabinets, gas bottle racks, roof
  racks, stacked and strapped crates, and cranes with slewing rings, rams and hook blocks.
- Helicopters stand on trailing-arm gear and tail wheels with real struts; aircraft carry detailed bombs,
  flare dispensers, formation lights, refuelling receptacles and chin-gun housings. Boats have bow eyes and
  hung fenders.
- Seat backs lean back rather than toward the people sitting in them, and the Merkava loader's machine gun
  stands on its mount instead of floating above the roof.
- Every gun still fires from exactly the same point.

screenshots.caption: Matched close-ups: before on the left, after on the right.

entries.title: Oil drums, spare-wheel carriers and fitted windows, doors and hatches
entries.summary: Vehicles carry proper 200-litre drums and hang their spare wheels on real carriers, and hundreds of windows, doors, hatches, sights, fuel tanks and gun mounts that were drawn by hand now use the shared, detailed versions.
entries.body:
- 200-litre drums on the T-55's rear plate and in the trucks' cargo loads have rolled rims, rolling hoops,
  filler bungs and steel straps.
- Spare wheels hang on real carriers: hub plates on doors and cab backs, the Hunter's swing-out arm, cradles
  with U-bolts behind cabs and on platforms, and a ratchet strap in the technical's bed. No spare floats any more.
- Vision blocks and door windows sit in rubber seals; doors, gear doors and hatches have hinges and handles;
  sights, radar panels, fuel tanks, bumpers, gun pintles and cannon barrels match across every army.
- Fixed along the way: the HEMTT repair truck's tool lockers no longer sit inside its rear wheels, and door
  seams on the Xian and Caesar lie on the skin instead of standing off it.

screenshots.caption: Matched close-ups: before on the left, after on the right.

entries.title: Lighter vehicle models
entries.summary: Every vehicle model now has about 45% less geometry and builds about 38% faster, and looks the same.
entries.body:
- The parts every vehicle shares (tyres, bolts, hinges, lamps, shackles, smoke dischargers, lockers and dozens
  more) were rebuilt to draw only what can be seen: hidden caps and inner faces are gone, small parts use fewer
  segments, and bends no longer carry a ball at every joint. Side-by-side renders of every vehicle family differ
  on at most 0.03% of pixels.
- Measured across all 135 vehicle models on one machine (Godot 4.7.2, team 0, seed 3, two runs each): geometry
  fell from 33.1 million to 18.5 million vertices, and building every model from cold took 16.3 seconds instead
  of 26.4. GPU time per frame on the vehicle roster scenario barely moved (13.8 to 13.1 ms at the median, within
  run-to-run noise), so expect smoother vehicle spawns rather than a higher frame rate on that scene.
- Searchlights show their lens: a solid collar used to hide it.

entries.title: Tactical numbers, insignia, welds and glass
entries.summary: Tanks and armoured vehicles carry tactical numbers and welded, chamfered armour; aircraft wear national insignia, bort numbers and exhaust soot; cars get tinted glass, pressed-metal bonnets and trim.
entries.body:
- Tanks, infantry fighting vehicles and APCs carry tactical numbers on their turrets or hull sides. On CSAT
  and independent armour the number changes from vehicle to vehicle, and it burns off a wreck.
- Hull and turret edges are chamfered or welded, so they catch the light instead of ending in a knife edge.
  The Namer family carries rows of bolted armour modules, the Merkava's wedge turret shows its plate seams,
  and tanks get tow cables along their guards, rolled tarps on their decks and soot behind their exhausts.
- Aircraft wear national insignia on wings, fins and booms, with serials, bort numbers or civil
  registrations, panel joints and exhaust soot. CSAT's jets now wear camouflage instead of flat sand.
- Car glass is tinted and glossy, with seats and a dark cabin behind it, instead of reading as an open
  frame. Bonnets and roofs catch light like pressed metal, with shut lines, black trim, B-pillars and proper
  tail-lamp clusters. Van and truck windows reflect the sky, and boat hulls are smoothly faired.
- Armoured glass on the Humvee and Hunter has a green tint.

screenshots.caption: Matched close-ups: before on the left, after on the right. The Varsuk, Kuma, Namer, Merkava, a hatchback, a minibus, the Shikra and the Kajman.

entries.title: Mud, stencils, car wheels and real track links
entries.summary: Armour carries mud and dust low on its hull and running gear and stencilled numbers that change from vehicle to vehicle; US vehicles wear bumper codes; cars roll on alloys and plastic trims; Russian-style tracks have single-pin links; glass reflects the sky; helicopter rotors blur into a disc.
entries.body:
- Armour and trucks carry wet mud low on the hull, wheels and tracks, with a ragged splash line and paler
  dust above it that settles on the upper faces. Cars pick up road dust along their sills and boats a
  waterline stain. The mud stays put on a turning wheel and moves with a traversing turret.
- Tactical numbers are stencilled in heavy bars in a worn army paint instead of bright white. Every NATO,
  CSAT and independent vehicle carries its own number. US Army vehicles also wear bumper codes for their
  battalion and company ("2-34 AR", "B24"), front and back.
- Cars roll on car wheels: low-profile tyres on five- or six-spoke alloys, or domed plastic trims on small
  cars and vans, instead of truck rims. Parked cars show their wheels under black arch trims.
- Russian-style tracks (CSAT's armour and the T-55) have cast single-pin links with a guide horn on every
  link, running between twin-ringed sprockets. Western tracks have rubber pads and end connectors, with
  centre guides on the Leopard 2, Warrior and Wiesel.
- Vehicle glass reflects the sky and the sun instead of reading as a flat black panel from above.
- A helicopter's rotor blurs into a soft disc in flight, with a faint ring at its tips and ghost blades
  that no longer flicker. Jets and gunships carry gun-gas and exhaust soot. The NATO Blackfish now wears
  its insignia and serials.

screenshots.caption: Matched close-ups: before on the left, after on the right. The Kuma, Abrams, Bradley, Kamysh, Merkava, Marshall, an SUV and a minibus.

entries.title: Rotor discs, rusted wrecks and each crew's own kit
entries.summary: A helicopter's rotor reads from above as a soft disc instead of a pale ring; burnt-out hulks and gutted cars turn to rust, ash and soot instead of black shapes; trucks and armour carry their own crew's load and tarps; hulls, bonnets and cabins get edges that catch the light.
entries.body:
- A helicopter's main rotor blurs into a soft, darker disc that you can see from the battle camera, with faint
  blade streaks and a soft edge, instead of a thin pale ring that looked like a selection circle. Tail rotors,
  the Blackfoot's and Orca's ducted fans, drones' rotors and aircraft propellers blur too instead of strobing.
- Burnt-out hulks on the map and gutted cars turn rust-brown with grey ash on their upper faces, scorched
  paint low down, and soot streaking up their sides, instead of featureless black shapes. A gutted car's
  tyres burn down to the wire, and the windows are sooty empty frames. A hulk that catches fire again only
  blackens in patches.
- Each crew stows its own load. Trucks of one kind carry different tarps and stacks of crates, with some
  ammunition already issued. Bags, bedrolls, jerrycans and ammo cans come in mixed colours. Canvas tilts
  differ in shade from truck to truck.
- Roofs, bonnets, consoles and superstructures have chamfered edges that catch the light: the Hunter's and
  Prowler's bonnets, the HEMTT's nose, boat consoles and the patrol ship's and trawler's deckhouses.

screenshots.caption: Matched studio views: before on the left, after on the right. A supply helicopter and the Blackfish in flight, a Marshall wreck, a burnt-out car, the Hunter's bonnet, and two Zamak ammo trucks.

entries.title: Wrecks that look burnt out
entries.summary: A destroyed vehicle now burns out properly: the fire spreads over the whole hull, leaving charred steel, rust and ash, and shot-down helicopters lie crashed and broken.
entries.body:
- **Burnt out, end to end:** every wreck, from tanks and APCs to trucks, technicals and helicopters, burns out from
  where the fire took hold. Over the best part of a minute the burn creeps across the hull, leaving charred steel,
  rust running down the sides, soot streaks and ash on the tops, with a few islands of blistered paint.
- **Embers:** while it burns, embers glow in the seams around the heart of the fire.
- **What burns away:** tyres burn off and wheeled vehicles sit down on their rims, canvas covers are gone, the grass
  around the wreck is burnt flat and the ground blackened, and torn-off pieces lie round it.
- **Crashed helicopters:** the blades shatter as they hit the ground: stubs at the hub, others snapped and bent into
  the dirt, some flung clear, and the tail rotor is usually gone. A helicopter that spun in lies rolled onto its side
  with its nose dug in; one that autorotated to a heavy landing sits slumped on its belly.

screenshots.caption: The same tank, technical and helicopter, two minutes after they were knocked out, before (top) and after (bottom).
The same two shoot-downs before (top) and after (bottom): a spin-in and a heavy landing, close up and from the commander's camera.

entries.title: Meter boxes, air conditioners and house numbers on the walls
entries.summary: House walls now carry the things real ones do: meter boxes, outside taps, air conditioners, satellite dishes, and by the front door a number, a letterbox and a mat.
entries.body:
- **Services**: about one plain wall in four has a meter cabinet (with the duct its cable comes up in, or a gas box on the ground), an outside tap with a hose coiled beside it, an air conditioner on wall brackets or on a pad at the foot of the wall, or a satellite dish on an arm.
- **At the front door**: most houses have their number on a plate beside the door, many a letterbox, and half a mat on the step.
- Barns get only a meter and a tap. It's all part of the wall it's fixed to, with no collision of its own, so cover and movement are unchanged.

screenshots.caption: A house from the front corner and a street of houses, before and after

entries.title: Walls that have seen the war
entries.summary: Town walls carry the marks of the fighting and the weather: bullet strikes, shell hits blown through to the brick, soot over burned-out windows, rain streaks, and windows taped, boarded or sandbagged.
entries.body:
- **Bullet strikes**: about one wall in five has taken a burst of fire, flakes of render knocked off round dark holes.
- **Shell hits**: now and then the render is blown off a wall to the brick behind it, scorched round and spattered with strikes.
- **Soot** climbs the wall above the odd window or door where a fire burned inside, fading into the paint.
- **Rain streaks** run down from the ends of many window sills.
- **Windows**: some lived-in houses have taped their glass in crosses, some windows are boarded across, and some have sandbags laid along the sill.
- It's all on the face of the wall: cover, movement and lines of fire are unchanged, and a boarded window still has gaps to see and shoot through.

screenshots.caption: The same house and street from the same cameras, before and after

entries.title: Roofs that have weathered
entries.summary: Tiled roofs grow moss and lichen, and flat roofs carry rain stains, patched membrane, moss along their parapets and vent pipes, so the town from above looks lived under for years.
entries.body:
- **Moss and lichen** grow in mottled patches on tiled roofs, mostly on the back slope: dark green where it stays damp, pale yellow-grey where it's dry.
- **Flat roofs** have dark rings where rain stood in the hollows (some green with algae), patches of newer membrane over old leaks, moss along the foot of a parapet, and a vent pipe or two.
- It's all on the roof's surface and fades into it, and roofs are still scenery only.

screenshots.caption: Tiled and flat roofs, and the town from above, before and after

entries.title: Layered woodland
entries.summary: Scanned trees, shrubs and undergrowth give woods a more natural shape, with leaf-covered soil, deadwood and small butterflies.
entries.body:
Broadleaf trees and two mature fir shapes use scanned trunks and branches, with irregular crowns and rooted bases. Shrubs, bracken, nettles and young pines form patches beneath them. Leaf-and-moss soil connects the stand, interrupted by fallen trunks, stumps, stones, loose leaves and small brown mushrooms.

Small tortoiseshell butterflies flutter near the undergrowth in daylight and golden-hour weather. Rain and the Wildlife setting hide them without rearranging the surrounding plants. The new ground details follow the terrain and avoid roads, buildings, water and barren slopes. They add no obstacles or cover, and follow grass quality; the forest soil remains with grass disabled.

screenshots.caption: Before above, after below: a generated woodland at eye level (left) and the forest floor (right). Each pair uses the same seed and camera, captured from the parent revision and the updated game.
Weathered wood, bracken and forest soil, young pines and shrubs, and the canopy in golden-hour light.

videos.caption: A small butterfly flutters above the woodland floor. Six seconds at normal speed, without sound.

entries.title: A faster Windows installer
entries.summary: The Windows installer unpacks the game in seconds instead of sitting on a stuck progress bar for a minute or more. The download is about 4% bigger.
entries.body:
- **Installing** takes seconds: the game is packed in a way that unpacks many times faster.
- **The progress** shown while it copies the game now counts up as it goes.

entries.title: Make the GPU benchmark clear about Time passes
entries.summary: The stationary GPU benchmark now marks Time passes as unmeasured instead of implying that it can price a moving sky while the battle clock is held.
entries.body: The report still compares the other graphics settings and restores every setting without saving. Time passes is listed separately, with an explanation that its sky relighting, terrain-shadow rebakes and reflection recaptures need an advancing battle clock. This fixes the benchmark's Cinematic coverage check without claiming a zero cost or a new performance measurement.

entries.title: Heat haze no longer floods the error log
entries.summary: With heat haze on, every vehicle destroyed while burning logged an error every frame for four minutes, thousands a minute, and sent them in error reports. It's quiet now.
entries.body:
- A destroyed vehicle's own fire no longer counts as heat once the vehicle is cleared away: its wreck burns, and shimmers, in its place.
- How the haze looks is unchanged.

entries.title: Clearer helicopter selections and a better crew pose
entries.summary: A selected helicopter’s footprint follows the ground around the aircraft. At a mortar pit, the crew member’s gloves meet the model.

screenshots.caption: The selected Mohawk on its landing pad and the crew member at the mortar pit, from the same cameras before and after.

entries.title: Meadow grass and bushes stand out again
entries.summary: Open fields show their tall grass tufts and leafy bushes from the battle camera again, instead of looking mown flat.
entries.body:
- Grass blades in open fields are broad enough to see from a commander's height again.
- Bushes scattered across meadows are full, leafy shrubs again; ferns, nettles, saplings and shrubs under the trees
  are unchanged.

screenshots.caption: Before above, after below: the same seed and camera. Grass tufts and leafy bushes are back in the fields; the undergrowth beneath the trees is unchanged.

entries.title: Doors, gear, arches and muzzles that fit
entries.summary: Helicopter gear hangs from the fuselage, every gun shows a dark bore, armoured cars' wheel arches are welded on, and doors, hatches and cranes fit their vehicles.
entries.body:
- Left-hand doors on the BTR, Sochor, MB 4WD, van and every fitted door, and the gear doors of the A-10,
  Wipeout, AC-130 and Blackfish, had their inside face or hinges turned outward; they mirror the right-hand side.
- Deck hatches on the RHIB and the patrol ship lie on the slope instead of sinking one edge into it, and the
  Merkava and Namer glacis access panels are hinged hatches.
- The Offroad and the technical tow on a ball hitch, the civilian 4x4 and truck have painted tow hooks, the
  Stomper's sensor mast leans as it should, and the Angara's Afghanit dischargers are proper launch tubes.
- Helicopter main gear hangs from fittings on the fuselage: the Ghost Hawk's, Black Hawk's, Apache's and
  Kajman's drag beams and shock struts used to end in mid-air beside it.
- Every gun's muzzle shows a dark bore instead of a grey disc, and the Sochor's and Scorcher's muzzle brakes
  read as open.
- The Ifrit's, Qilin's and Typhoon's faceted wheel arches are one band welded to the hull instead of three
  loose planks, the Zamak repair truck's folded crane clears its body's roof, and the Xian's missile tubes
  are a packed launcher on cradles under the stub wing.

releases.name: Cinematic lighting
releases.summary: A new Cinematic graphics preset: a sky worked out from real sunlight scattering, shadows from fires and flares, sun shafts, lens flare, eye adaptation and a film look. Close-up shadows are sharper on every preset from Medium up.

entries.title: Cinematic lighting
entries.summary: A new Cinematic graphics preset: a sky worked out from real sunlight scattering, shadows from fires and flares, sun shafts, lens flare, eye adaptation and a film look. Close-up shadows are sharper on every preset from Medium up.
entries.body:
Pick **Cinematic** at the top of Settings, or turn each part on by itself. Cinematic is everything Ultra has, plus all of this; it's meant for a fast graphics card, screenshots and replays. None of it changes the battle itself: spotting, cover and fire work as before.

- **Adaptive shadows** (Graphics, on from Medium up): the sun's shadows are fitted to the ground the camera can see instead of always reaching 800 m out, so close in they're several times sharper. Costs next to nothing.
- **Shadows from fire and flares** (Graphics): explosions, burning wrecks, illumination flares and street lamps throw moving shadows, the two or six nearest the camera.
- **Physical sky** (Graphics): at golden hour, dawn, dusk and in haze, the sky is worked out from how sunlight scatters in the air: deep blue overhead, a small reddened sun, pink-lit clouds, the earth's shadow rising at dusk. It lights the battlefield too, so shade turns sky-blue while the sunlit side glows.
- **Camera and lens** (Lighting & Look):
  - **Lens flare and glare**: bright lights throw ghosts and a halo through the lens, the hottest ones a thin streak, and light up dust on the glass.
  - **Sun shafts**: light streaming past trees, ridges and smoke that stand against a low sun.
  - **Local exposure**: keeps the detail in deep shade and in bright fire at the same time, as the eye does.
  - **Eye adaptation**: the view dims for a flash and recovers after it, and in the dark colour drains towards a cool grey as night vision takes over.
  - **Film look**: highlights bleed red into the film, and fine detail is sharpened without halos.
- The camera and lens effects and the physical sky aren't in the browser version, whose graphics can't draw them.

screenshots.caption: The same camera, seed and moment on Ultra (left) and Cinematic (right): looking into a dawn sun, a night battle round burning wrecks, golden hour; and a tank barrel's shadow close in on High, with adaptive shadows off and on.

entries.title: Photo mode
entries.summary: F9 holds a solo battle or a replay still, puts the interface away and frees the camera, with a real lens, the light and a film look to set before you take the picture.
entries.body:
- **The action holds still** in a solo battle or a replay. In multiplayer the fighting goes on: only your camera
  comes off.
- **A free camera:** WASD fly the way the lens looks, E / Q go up and down, Z / C roll (Backspace levels it), and
  holding a mouse button and dragging looks round. Shift flies faster, Ctrl slower, the wheel zooms. It stays
  above the ground and over the map.
- **The lens:** field of view, where it focuses and how soft the rest falls, as real depth of field (not in the
  browser, whose renderer has none).
- **The light and the film:** exposure, the time of day, a colour grade with its contrast and saturation, vignette
  and grain. The fog of war's shading can come off the ground too.
- **Camera and lens:** lens flare, sun shafts, local exposure, eye adaptation, the film look and heat haze switch on
  and off for the picture alone, whatever your graphics settings have (on the desktop).
- **Space takes the picture** without the panel, at twice the resolution for cleaner edges, as a PNG in the
  game's screenshots folder, and a note says where. In a browser it's downloaded.
- **F2 hides the panel. F9 or Esc puts everything back** as it was, the battle's speed included. Your settings are
  never touched.
- Every key is in **Settings → Controls**, under Photo mode.

screenshots.caption: Photo mode over a held moment at Beachhead: the lens focused on the stone house at 22 m, flare, sun shafts, film look and heat haze on
The picture it saved: no panel, drawn at twice the resolution and scaled down

entries.title: Command by intent: hand squads to your XO
entries.summary: Select squads or vehicles, press I and give them an intent: hold a sector, take an objective, screen, wait in reserve or ambush a road. Your XO places them, gives their orders, sends them in again when they're knocked back, and reports over the radio.
entries.body:
You don't have to run every squad yourself any more. **I** opens the Delegate page of the orders; pick an intent,
click the place (drag toward the enemy to set the front), and the squads are your XO's to run.

- **Hold sector:** spread across it and dug in; a squad knocked off its piece of the line is put back.
- **Take objective:** a deliberate attack, one squad firing while the others flank, then they consolidate and hold
  it. A failed attack is sent in again, a few times, before the XO reports that it has stalled. A click near a
  town aims at its square.
- **Screen:** a thin line well forward that reports what's coming and falls back a bound at a time when pressed.
- **Reserve:** waits out of the fight and goes to help a squad of yours nearby that's pinned or bleeding, joining
  its attack, then comes back.
- **Ambush:** each squad lays an ambush on the nearest road, springs it, slips away and lays it again.
- **Taking them back:** give a delegated squad any order of your own, or press **Shift + I**, and it's yours again.
  The XO says so on the radio. A squad cut down to a third is sent back to refit and handed back to you.
- On the map each intent shows with an XO tag, its grid and what it's doing; delegated squads carry an XO tab,
  and the order of battle and squad card say what they've been told.
- **AI allies answer your pings.** With an AI commander on your side, "attack here", "defend here" and "need
  support" pings now get up to two of its free squads sent there, and it tells you who's coming (or that nobody is
  free).
- Co-commanders delegate and take back the same way, and every allied player sees the XO's tasks.

screenshots.caption: Three squads told to take the farmyard: the XO plans a deliberate attack, a base of fire and a flanking assault. The order of battle and the squad card read XO TAKE.
The same platoon told to hold a sector: dug in across it, the sector's forward edge drawn on the ground, and the Delegate page of the orders open.

entries.title: Heat haze
entries.summary: On the Cinematic preset the air shimmers over fires and burning wrecks, over the engines of idling tanks and helicopters, and for a moment round a blast.
entries.body:
Turn it on by itself under **Settings > Lighting & Look > Camera and lens > Heat haze**, or pick the **Cinematic** preset.

- **What shimmers:** burning wrecks, buildings, woods and grass fires; the engine decks and exhausts of vehicles with their engines running, harder while they drive; a helicopter's turbines, the haze beaten down once its rotor is up to speed; and briefly round a blast, a tank gun's muzzle and a rocket's back-blast.
- Only what lies behind the hot air is bent: a soldier standing in front of a fire stays sharp, and the sky is left alone.
- Nearer haze bends more, and haze too small to make out from far away isn't drawn.
- With **Reduce motion** on, the air holds still: the view is still bent, but nothing swims.
- It's looks only: spotting, cover and fire work as before. Like the other camera and lens effects, it isn't in the browser version.

videos.caption: A tank that has just brewed up burns behind two idling tanks: the air over the wreck and over their engine decks swims, first from the usual battle camera, then close over an engine deck.

entries.title: Shot-down helicopters fall out of the sky
entries.summary: A helicopter shot down in the air no longer vanishes into a pile of rubble below: it spins in or autorotates to a crash, and its burning wreck lies where it hit.
entries.body:
- **Spinning in:** with the tail rotor or the controls shot away, the helicopter winds up into a spin, rolling and
  pitching as it corkscrews down, and hits hard, still carrying its speed.
- **Autorotation:** with only the engines gone, the pilot glides it down steeply, nose low, then flares just above
  the ground for a heavy landing. More of the troops aboard walk away from this kind of crash.
- **The impact** is a fuel explosion that hurts whoever is underneath and can set the area alight. The burnt-out
  helicopter is left lying where it hit, on its side after a spin-in. Over deep water it ditches and sinks, and the
  survivors swim for shore.
- On the way down it burns and trails smoke, and its rotor runs down.

videos.caption: Two Ghost Hawks shot down at 16 m, before (top) and after (bottom), at normal speed. The near one loses its tail rotor and spins in; the far one autorotates to a heavy landing. The yellow lines trace their paths.

entries.title: Houses that look lived in, and lamplight at night
entries.summary: Curtains, blinds and nets hang in the windows, flowers sit on sills, lanterns hang by front doors and aerials stand on roofs. Inside are painted walls, pictures, shelves and rugs, and at dusk and at night lamps glow behind a third of the windows.
entries.body:
- **Windows:** drapes drawn to the sides, a blind half down, or nets across the lower panes. Some windows have
  flowers in a box on the sill. Houses still lived in keep their glass.
- **Doors and roofs:** a lantern beside about half the front doors, and a TV aerial on half the pitched roofs,
  lashed to the chimney or standing on the ridge.
- **Inside:** you see the rooms when a roof lifts for the men inside, and in every roofless ruin. They have
  painted walls with a skirting, a radiator under each window, and pictures, a mirror, a clock or a shelf of
  books on the plain walls. Most floors have a rug. Everything hangs flat on the walls or lies flat on the
  floor, so nothing stands where your men take cover.
- **At dusk and at night** a lamp is on behind about a third of the windows. The barracks and research post
  windows glow, and so do the factory's north lights and the door lanterns. Brightest at night, a glimmer on an
  overcast or rainy day, nothing in sunshine. The light changes with Settings > Time of day.

screenshots.caption: Matched before and after: a house under the same studio camera by day, with its roof off as when your men are inside, and by night; then a house in the town on the same seed and camera.

entries.title: Ride along with the object cameras
entries.summary: Select one vehicle, building or individual soldier and press F10 to cycle through its camera positions. Escape returns to command with the selection intact.
entries.body:
Every subject offers a rear and aerial view. Vehicles with tracks or wheels have a low running-gear view. Models can also carry cameras on the barrel, beside the roof gun and over the engine deck. Rotorcraft add a cabin-side view. On sling-capable helicopters the sling-load view keeps the aircraft and its cargo in frame. Boats have bow and waterline views. The tanks use the same mounts used in the one-minute ridge film. Change the key in Settings under Controls.

The waterline view follows the wake from the stern quarter. It keeps the horizon level as the boat turns. The sling camera frames the rotor against the sky, with the suspended vehicle and its shadow visible below.

From the cargo door, look down past the landing gear and watch the sling load separate from its shadow. Wheels stop throwing dust once clear of the ground. Spinning rotors show a soft sweep for each blade. On the RHIB, the starboard camera looks past the console toward the other boats.

screenshots.caption: Six positions on the ridge. The low track view follows the suspension, the barrel view looks back toward the turret, and the roof camera stays beside the mounted gun.

videos.caption: The same lift and boat turn from both camera positions. The new views on the right show the gap below the cargo and the wake behind the stern.
The same lift in both views. On the right the rotor turns against the sky and the Humvee clears its shadow below.

entries.title: Standing orders for squads, soldiers and vehicles
entries.summary: Tell a squad or one soldier to get down or hold their fire, tell a tank what to shoot first, pop a vehicle's smoke yourself, and drop only some of the men a carrier has aboard.
entries.body:
- **Stance** (K): auto, prone, crouch or stand, for a whole squad or one soldier you've picked out (Alt + click).
  Told to stay down, men crawl when they move at a walk; a run order still gets them up. A pinned man won't stand
  up whatever he's told, and diving from a grenade or hitting the dirt is still his own call.
- **Fire discipline** (J): fire at will, return fire (only once they or their squad are shot at) or hold fire. Men
  holding their fire throw no grenades and fire no rockets either, but they still fight anyone who gets within
  15 m, and anything you tell them to attack. Squads under either order keep moving past enemies they only see.
- **Vehicles** take the same fire discipline (the crew still fights anything within 22 m), and a **target
  priority** (N): armour first saves the main gun for vehicles, infantry first puts high explosive on men in the
  open.
- **Smoke on call** (T with only vehicles selected): the dischargers fire towards the nearest threat; the card shows
  the salvoes left. The crew still pops smoke by itself when a missile is launched at it.
- **Partial dismount**: drop half the men aboard, or one squad when a carrier holds two. The rest stay in until you
  dismount them (U) or the vehicle moves on and stops again; if it's badly hit, everyone bails out.
- Every order sticks until you change it, through moves and attacks, and the command card shows what's in force.

screenshots.caption: A squad behind a wall told to keep low and only return fire: the command card shows both orders in force
An IFV carrying two squads: smoke salvoes left, dismount everyone, half, or one squad, and its fire and target orders

entries.title: A Field Manual on the website, over the menus' living map
entries.summary: The website sits on the menus' topographic map now. Home always shows the game off, and the new Manual covers every soldier, squad, weapon, vehicle, building, fire mission and upgrade, with the game's figures and 3D models.
entries.body:
- **Home** replaces The game in the header, and its tour greets everyone. Signed in, your rank, progress and Play sit just under the footage.
- **Manual** replaces Vehicles. Its overview explains how the game fights: command, drills, the two sides, combined arms, building, supply, fire support and the battlefield. Infantry, Vehicles, Buildings, Fire support and Research follow.
- Filter a chapter by kind and by side, search it, and share a link to any entry. The figures are the game's own, with the in-game manual's counted bars.
- Turn over the 3D model of any building, squad, soldier, weapon or fire mission, as well as vehicles. Fire support plays an aircraft's sortie too.
- Every page sits on the menus' living topographic map. It drifts, leans a little after the cursor and ripples where you click. It holds still if you prefer reduced motion.
- Fixed: a page you hadn't opened yet, such as your profile, could fail to load in a tab left open across a website update. That tab now reloads onto the new version.
- Old Vehicles links open the Manual's Vehicles.

layoutComparison.caption: Website layout comparison at 1600 x 900, the rank guide. Before: the live website on 11 November 2026, on a still picture of the map. After: the same page on the living map, quieter behind the text. Viewport captures, not gameplay comparisons.

screenshots.caption: The Field Manual: how the game fights, chapter by chapter, and a way into every catalogue.
Buildings, squads, soldiers, weapons and fire missions have the game's own figures and 3D model, as vehicles do.

entries.title: Ride with the Abrams and T-55A
entries.summary: Ride beside the tracks, look down the barrel or watch through the periscope in a match. Disabled tanks keep their paint and turret bearing as smoke rises from the engine deck.
entries.body: A glancing round rings against the hull. The barrel recoils when the gun fires, and individual tread pads leave prints on soft ground. Select a tank and press F10 to cycle its views.

screenshots.caption: The same turn before (left) and after (right), with the ground enlarged below. Separate tread pads press into the soil.

videos.caption: The playable Abrams in an ordinary match. Three in-game F10 mounts show the tracks, periscope and barrel during the same seeded encounter.
The same 2.5 seconds of the knockout in both cuts. On the right, hot folds rise through the engine grille and darken into the plume.

entries.title: Broken earth at ground impacts
entries.summary: Larger clods of earth tumble with uneven edges as the dust rises around them.
entries.body: The larger pieces bounce and settle back onto the ground. Their paths vary between recordings.

videos.caption: The same round lands beyond the wreck. Watch the larger clods above the dust in the previous version on the left and the updated version on the right.

entries.title: Hear the jet pass overhead
entries.summary: The engine follows the jet across the scene, and falling bombs carry a separate rush of air into the impact.
entries.body: Listen from the harbour and the engine grows louder as the aircraft passes, then fades into the distance. From a camera flying beside the jet, its engine stays with it. Close to the aircraft, a short mechanical clack marks each release. Air rushes past the falling bombs until impact.

videos.caption: The same harbour pass plays twice. The updated audio starts at 0:05.8. Listen under the wing for the release, then from the quay for the falling air.

entries.title: Battle readouts that read over any ground
entries.summary: The log, fire missions and squad names on the map stay legible over sunlit grass, sand and smoke, and the log no longer slides under the observer's bar.
entries.body:
- **Darker outlines** round every readout on the battlefield, so small text holds up over bright terrain and smoke.
- **Message times** and **fire mission cooldowns** are drawn a step brighter; cooldowns could all but vanish on grass.
- **Squad names on the map** are a size larger and brighter.
- **Watching a battle**, the message log starts below the observer's bar instead of running underneath it.
- The order of battle's key is shown in a key box, like every other key on screen.

screenshots.caption: The same moments before and after: the message log, the order of battle and the fire missions over bright ground

entries.title: See into the Black Wasp cockpit
entries.summary: Catch the pilot’s helmet through the curved canopy as a Black Wasp flies past.
entries.body: The bronze coating catches the light along the rim. Looking down through the canopy reveals the seat back, helmet and visor.

screenshots.caption: The same flypast seen from the same camera. The former canopy is on the left. On the right, the pilot and seat show through the coating.

entries.title: See the water from the stern and bridge
entries.summary: Select a boat and press F10 to reach Stern quarter. The horizon stays level as the hull rolls. On the patrol ship, Bridge roof looks down on boats passing the port rail.

videos.caption: The same harbour pass from Waterline on the left and Stern quarter on the right. Watch where the first splash breaks above the cabin.
One pass at the same moment. The bow view on the left shows the patrol ship. From the bridge roof on the right, the smaller boat and its wake pass below the rail.

entries.title: Buildings built from shared parts
entries.summary: Houses, huts, sheds and defences now share one set of walls, roofs, windows, doors, fittings and wire. Roofs sit on their walls, gutters and downpipes take the rain, and the town has brick and stone houses among the rendered ones.
entries.body:
- **Roofs sit on the walls.** The eave walls no longer show through the tiles, and the gable ends no longer
  show along the verges. Pitched roofs have fascias, barge boards, a round ridge, gutters and swan-necked
  downpipes; chimneys have an oversailing course and their pots.
- **Brick and stone houses** stand among the rendered ones. Each house is dressed in its own material:
  concrete sills and lintels on brick, a keystone over stone windows, darker plinths, a band under the eaves.
- **Windows and doors:** framed windows with panes whole, cracked to shards or gone, louvred or boarded
  shutters, door steps, the odd hood over a front door, ledged doors on the barracks, steel doors on bunkers
  and the research post.
- **Military buildings:** the barracks in lapped weatherboard under lapped sheeting, the factory with real
  north lights, a roller shutter and pipes on brackets, the research post in jointed panels with ribbon glazing.
  Masts are guyed, and the factory's flag has a pole.
- **Common things are shared:** flat roofs have coped parapets, scuppers and downpipes. Garden walls have
  saddleback or brick-on-edge copings. The same drums, crates and pallets turn up at FOBs, dumps, barricades,
  caches and the dock. Tents, tarps and nets are pegged out, utility poles carry insulators, and compound
  walls carry barbed wire.
- None of this changes cover, collision or sight lines. House walls build in about the same time as before
  with fewer meshes.

screenshots.caption: Matched before and after: a house in the town on the same seed and camera, then a house, the barracks and the factory under the same studio camera.
The shared parts on their own: wall finishes, roofs, windows, doors, shutters, rainwater goods, plant, masts, stores and wire.

entries.title: Cloud shadows fall on everything
entries.summary: The drifting shade of the clouds now darkens soldiers, vehicles, buildings, trees and roads along with the ground, so a tank parked in it no longer stands out sunlit.
entries.body:
- **Everything in the shade darkens:** soldiers, tanks and every other vehicle, houses and works, trees, hedges,
  grass, stones, roads and trenches, by as much as the ground beneath them.
- **Only the sunlight goes:** the sky still lights what stands in the shade, so the side of a house that was already
  in its own shadow stays as it was.
- **It moves with the wind**, the same way as the smoke.
- **In the browser** the clouds now shade the ground too (they never did there before), and everything on it.
- **Graphics setting:** *Cloud shadows on everything*, on from the High preset up. Off, only the ground, grass and
  bushes darken, as before.

screenshots.caption: The same moment with the new setting off (as before) and on: in the cloud's shade, the tank and the walls of the house now darken with the ground around them.

videos.caption: A cloud's shade drifting over a parked tank and a hamlet, at twice real speed, with the setting off (as before) and on. On, the tank and the walls go into the shade and out of it with the ground.

entries.title: The field medic moves with the squad
entries.summary: The Coalition medic wears the squad’s textured uniform, with a marked sleeve and an aid pack that move with him.
entries.body: Look for the white band on his left arm. His pack follows his shoulders as he walks and crouches.

videos.caption: The medic crosses the Sky Hook landing pad beside the squad leader. The previous model is on the left and the updated model is on the right.

entries.title: Coalition riflemen wear their SWAT kit by default
entries.summary: Close-up riflemen now use the character and animations included with Frontline as soon as you start a battle.

screenshots.caption: Coalition riflemen in the casualty drill with the bundled SWAT kit
The same drill previously used the procedural infantry models

entries.title: Water impacts fall back into the harbour
entries.summary: Tall sheets of spray rise beside boats and fall back into the spreading foam.
entries.body:
The slower spray stays near the surface while the faster sheets rise above it. Watch the water around the patrol ship as the sheets come back down.

Fast boats leave a widening patch of churned water behind their motors. The bow wave starts close to the hull as the boat turns.

videos.caption: The same harbour pass in both views. On the left the plumes drift out of frame. On the right their tips break apart and fall back around the ship.
Watch the stern of the boat crossing the bow. The earlier wake on the left leaves two thin trails. On the right the motors turn up a broadening patch of foam.

The same boat from the bridge roof. On the left a straight foam edge leads the bow and a brown disc flashes over the water. On the right the wake builds along the hull and the sea stays visible through the flash.

entries.title: Helicopters fly like helicopters
entries.summary: Helicopters tilt into every change of speed, bank round turns, climb away from the pad and come down a glide path into a low hover, throwing up dust as they land.
entries.body:
- **Tilt first, then speed:** the nose dips before a helicopter picks up speed and comes up into a flare before it
  slows, so you can read what it is about to do. Big transports answer the controls slowly; light scouts snap round.
- **Banked turns:** at speed the nose stays on the flight path and the helicopter banks round the turn. A sharp
  change of course is flown as a tight, slowing turn, not a stop and a pivot in mid-air.
- **Take-off:** the rotor winds up to speed first, then the helicopter lifts into a low hover, noses over and climbs
  away as it gathers speed, instead of rising straight up like a lift.
- **Landing:** it comes down a glide path, slowing all the way, into a low hover over the spot and sets down gently,
  instead of stopping high over the landing zone and sinking straight down.
- **Hovering:** a hovering helicopter hangs slightly nose-up with one side low and drifts gently as the pilot holds
  it, and its downwash throws a ring of dust (or spray over water) when it is low.
- **Sound:** the rotor's beat follows its speed as it winds up, and gets heavier in a hard flare or a steep bank.
- **Sling loads** swing on the cable: they lag behind as the helicopter accelerates and swing forward as it slows.
  The load is lowered from a hover and let go only once it has stopped swinging.
- **Gunships** fly to their firing position nose first, then swing round to face the target.

videos.caption: The same transport flight from a helipad beside a base, with a change of destination eight seconds in, before (top) and after (bottom), at normal speed. The yellow line traces the flight path, with a drop line to the ground every second.

entries.title: Military paint wear and material-aware vehicle panels
entries.summary: Military bodies gain clearer camouflage and worn panel edges. Truck canopies now use sewn cloth that sags between supports, with different construction for metal, fabric, rubber and glass.
entries.body:
- Military paint has broken edge rubs, small primer chips and restrained runoff streaks. Aircraft exterior paint is more matte.
- Vehicle camouflage has larger, more distinct colour patches. Civilian clearcoat and uniform camouflage retain their own treatment.
- HEMTT, Zamak and Tempest troop canopies share draped cloth bays with sewn hems. Tied cargo covers also gain perimeter hems.
- Panel construction follows the material: folded edges and fasteners for metal, hems and stitching for fabric, moulded edges for rubber and plastic, and seals for glass.
- These are shared construction and finish improvements; unique vehicle silhouettes remain authored separately.

screenshots.caption: After: more distinct camouflage, worn panel edges and cloth fitted between the canopy supports.
Before: the same truck with low-contrast mottling and a rigid canopy shell.
Shared construction examples: folded metal, sewn fabric, moulded rubber and plastic, wood and sealed glass.

entries.title: Mortar crews work the emplacement with both hands
entries.summary: The gunner kneels at the fixed mortar and puts away his carried tube while he works.
entries.body: Leaving the pit brings the gunner’s carried kit back into view.

videos.caption: The same round from the same camera. On the left the carried tube stays on the gunner’s back. On the right he works the single mortar in the pit.

entries.title: A closer look at the mortar crew
entries.summary: The Coalition mortar specialist wears the squad’s textured kit and keeps his carried equipment on his back as he moves.
entries.body: The carried kit follows the spine through the vault and crouch. On Macs using native OpenGL, squads use the articulated character models so bodies remain visible alongside their equipment.

videos.caption: The same specialist crosses the same sandbags from the same camera. The previous model is on the left and the updated one is on the right.

entries.title: Clouds and coastal horizons
entries.summary: Open valleys and lower playable hills lead through coastal water to towering distant ranges, cloud banks and ridge mist.
entries.body:
Cloud banks sit beyond the playable boundary, adding depth around distant peaks without changing spotting or movement. Their shaded billows and trailing mist follow the scene lighting, including rain and night. Mountains correctly hide clouds behind them, while stronger distant haze leaves the playable foreground clear.

Generated skirmish maps now occupy lower foothills, keeping the valley, roads and settlements visible instead of hiding them behind giant nearby peaks. The really tall mountain range stays in the distance. Mission terrain keeps its existing heights.

Coastal maps continue through a broad water channel to the distant ranges. The seeded shoreline and shallow seabed continue across the map edge without a projecting shelf or straight colour seam, and the ocean continues beyond the terrain backdrop. Inland maps retain their land backdrop.

Choose **Mountain clouds** in Graphics: Off, Low, Medium, High or Ultra. Standard presets select matching detail levels; browsers start at Low. Reduced motion stops the clouds drifting. Higher settings take more samples through each cloud; performance depends on the view and graphics card.

screenshots.caption: Matched wide view before and after the shoreline repair: the near coast continues into the scenery without the projecting shelf or straight colour boundary.

videos.caption: A fixed wide view across the valley in daylight, golden hour, rain and night. Native captures joined with short dissolves; these compare existing lighting moods.

entries.title: Burning pickups keep their paint beyond the bonnet
entries.summary: When a technical overturns, soot spreads from the engine across the original bodywork.
entries.body: The cab, wheels and bed remain visible around the fire as the wreck settles.

videos.caption: The same pickup and strike from the harbour side. The previous wreck finish is on the left, and the spreading engine soot is on the right.

entries.title: Browse updates one change at a time
entries.summary: Scan a compact release overview, open a change for its lead image or clip, then use Previous and Next to explore the release.
entries.body:
- Choose a release from the archive, then scan its compact titles and one-line summaries.
- Open any change to see its lead image or clip. Thumbnail galleries keep the remaining evidence close without playing every clip at once.
- Previous and Next move through the changes, with keyboard focus following the selection. Open the full details when you want the deeper explanation.
- Existing release and change links continue to work, including links opened from the game.
- Vehicle previews now explain startup failures, including unavailable WebGL, instead of hiding the error behind a loading message. Retry is available without leaving the roster.
- Release download instructions point to the Windows installer and Mac disk image and explain automatic updates.

layoutComparison.caption: Website layout comparison at 1440 x 1000. Before: the live website on 11 November 2026. After: the revised local page using the same v1.0.13 release content. Viewport captures, not gameplay comparisons.

screenshots.caption: One change open, with its lead image, a position in the release, and Previous/Next controls. Detailed notes stay optional.

entries.title: Ride behind the RHIB’s helmsman
entries.summary: Both launches have a driver at the controls. Press F10 on a selected RHIB to look over the helmsman’s right shoulder.
entries.body: The driver sits at the starboard console. From the Helm view you can follow the other boat across your bow and pick up its wake as it turns for shore.

videos.caption: The same boats making the same turn. The earlier starboard view is on the left. The new Helm view on the right keeps the driver and the crossing launch in sight.

entries.title: Tank tracks follow the crest
entries.summary: Individual shoes wrap around the road wheels as the Abrams, T-55 and Bradley cross uneven ground. Their engines stay audible at idle and the running gear grows louder as the tracks pick up speed.
entries.body:
The inner and outer tracks travel different distances through a turn. On both tanks, the main barrel slides back into its mount when it fires, while the suspension absorbs the kick. The T-55’s upper run sags between the wheels, and the two tanks have distinct engine notes.

Tracked vehicles stir a low trail of dust as the shoes lift off the road.

screenshots.caption: The previous wheel faces and track shoes on the same slope.
Stamped road wheels and hinged tread shoes in the same climb.

videos.caption: Follow the second Abrams on the same village road. On the right the dust spreads behind both treads and the impressions stay visible through it.

entries.title: Jagged crags on the hills
entries.summary: Bare rock on the hills breaks into knobs, ledges and clefts a few metres deep, so crests are jagged and rock faces have real relief up close.
entries.body:
- Steep bare rock now has knobs, ledges and clefts up to a few metres deep, finer than the hills' own shape, so crests break into a jagged line instead of a smooth dome.
- The distant mountains break into crags, ribs and gullies too, and their snowfields lie broken along them instead of in smooth sheets.
- **Alpine haze** (High and above) is lighter, so the far crags, snowfields and woods keep their detail while the ranges still stand apart from the sky. Pale scree gathers below the far crags too.
- Everything uses the same rock: men stand on it, it blocks sight and fire, and shells dig into it where they land.
- Routes over the hills are unchanged: the crags roughen the rock without making new paths impassable.
- Mission maps keep their terrain exactly as before.

screenshots.caption: The same crags before and after: at golden hour (seed 11) and by day (seed 3).

entries.title: Rain-cut gullies on the rock
entries.summary: Steep rock faces, on the hills and the distant mountains, are cut by gullies that run downhill and branch as they gather.
entries.body:
- Steep rock is scored by rain gullies, as real weathered faces are: they run straight downhill on every face and branch where they gather.
- Close up they are a few metres apart; on the distant mountains they are spaced like real ravines and soften with distance.
- This is a change of look only: the ground units stand and fight on is unchanged.

screenshots.caption: Before and after: a crag at golden hour, and a distant peak from a low camera (seed 11).

entries.title: Rolling valleys, carved hills and living meadows
entries.summary: Battlefield valleys roll instead of lying flat, hills climb out of the ground through stony shoulders and branching gullies, and meadows change with the land: lush in hollows and by the water, dry on crests.
entries.body:
- **The valley floor rolls.** Gentle rises and dips a few metres high run across the open ground, enough to hide a squad from a distant gun. Roads ride over them; towns, bases, rivers and ponds keep their level ground.
- **Hills look carved, not stamped.** They rise out of the plain on soft aprons, break into spurs and gullies where they meet a road or the shore, and lose the evenly combed flanks they used to have. Rock near and far now shares the same grey stone.
- **Meadows follow the land.** Grass stays lush in hollows, along drainage lines and beside rivers and ponds, and dries to straw on crests and slopes facing the sun. Pastures differ from one field to the next, and the grass tufts grow thicker and greener on damp ground.
- **Stony ground** lies between meadow and crag on hill shoulders, pale talus gathers at the foot of the crags, and rock seen close up keeps its cracks and grain. The muddy patches that slow men down now look like dark rutted soil.
- **Cloud shadows** are cloud-sized now, drifting slowly over the ground, grass and bushes, instead of small dark blotches that spotted every field.
- **Distant woods** grow in broad, ragged stands that climb the mountain gullies and fade into the haze with the slopes they stand on, instead of dark stripes along the far shore.
- Mission maps keep their terrain exactly as before.

screenshots.caption: The same views before and after (seed 3, day): the whole valley, a hill above the river, and a rock knob by a pond.

entries.title: Better-built guns, sights, hatches and lights across the roster
entries.summary: Machine guns, cannon, sights, cupolas, hatches, reactive armour, rotor masts, exhausts and lights now share one detailed design per part, used by every vehicle that carries them.
entries.body:
- Machine guns have proper receivers, perforated barrel jackets, carrying handles, spade grips and sealed
  ammunition cans with their belts; cannon have ported muzzle brakes, and miniguns and the A-10's GAU-8
  clamped barrel clusters. Missile tubes have end collars and covers.
- Turret rings are bolted, sight heads have framed windows under armoured visors, commander's cupolas have
  hooded vision blocks, and roof hatches sit on seals with hinges and handles. Reactive armour bricks have
  bolted covers, and tank guns' fume extractors taper onto the barrel.
- Helicopter rotor masts have bolted collars and their turbine exhausts are open, sooty pipes. Aircraft and
  boats show red to port and green to starboard in proper sidelights, with glossy beacons and masthead lights.
- Trucks have beaded, bolted fenders and strapped fuel tanks with filler caps; rolled tarps are strapped.
- Every gun still fires from exactly the same point. Twenty parts are now shared across more than a hundred
  vehicle models, so future improvements to any of them reach the whole roster at once.

entries.title: More convincing vehicle construction
entries.summary: Truck cabins, tanker bodies, windows, steps and recovery equipment have more fitted detail, with shared construction carrying improvements across related vehicles.
entries.body:
- Truck cabs gain fitted window surrounds, joined door hardware, raised wipers and gripped boarding treads. Tankers have rounded dished ends, straps and mounting saddles.
- Storage lids, armour skirt attachments, cargo restraints and recovery winches have more distinct construction. Aircraft gain recessed duct faces, hollow rocket tubes and detailed landing struts; boats share improved seats and mooring fittings.
- Thirty construction techniques now share builders across multiple vehicle designs. Some changes are subtle at normal camera distances; shared loft and profile code preserves the existing silhouettes while making later improvements easier.

screenshots.caption: Matched close-ups: before on the left, after on the right. Cab frames, tanker ends, recovery winches, helicopter glazing and rocket tubes, aircraft intakes, and boat seating.

entries.title: See the straps holding a sling load
entries.summary: Look down from a helicopter’s cargo door and follow all four straps to the vehicle below.
entries.body:
The cable moves with the helicopter’s belly as it banks. The straps have width and catch the light on the way down to the vehicle body. The suspended vehicle keeps its wheels and tracks still, and its suspension settles as it crosses a bank or bridge.

The cargo-door view follows the vehicle through the helicopter’s turns. When the straps come off, the camera looks back along its original sightline.

videos.caption: The same Sky Hook crossing, before on the left and after on the right. Watch the gap above the tracked vehicle as it passes over the bridge camera.
Watch the Nyx as it swings across the bridge. The older door camera is on the left. The new view follows the hull on the right.

entries.title: Trenches dug, used and repaired
entries.summary: Crews dig usable trenches in stages, with sloped entrances, fire steps and rear bays. Bombardment collapses individual sections that engineers can clear again.
entries.body:
- Construction leaves a shallow, usable ditch before the finished trench. Work remains when crews are interrupted; more workers help only while there is space to dig.
- Open ends slope to the surface, junctions stay connected, and duckboards follow the terrain. Fire steps and occasional supply or resting bays keep the passage clear.
- Uneven spoil, exposed soil and roots, muddy boot marks, supplies and broken timber give the works a lived-in appearance. Shovels lift and throw soil.
- Troops step aside in narrow passages and slow down to climb a high lip. Trench protection also works on elevated terrain.
- Shell damage fills individual sections with earth instead of deleting the trench. Engineers clear them using the existing repair order.
- Digging takes longer than before, scales with length, and is slower through compacted roads. Timber shelters offer modest physical cover, not bunker protection.

The defensive-battle scenario now carries its trench line across both flank emplacements.

screenshots.caption: The same trench network before and after: irregular earthwork, fire steps and recessed rear bays.

videos.caption: Engineers excavate a trench, then clear a damaged section. Controlled demonstration at normal simulation speed; damage is applied at 18 seconds.

entries.title: Shared antennas, mirrors and hollow gun barrels
entries.summary: Vehicle radio whips gain spring mounts, mirrors gain housings and reflective faces, and major tank and artillery guns gain open muzzles and segmented thermal sleeves.
entries.body:
- The core, NATO, CSAT and independent vehicle builders share tapered radio whips with bolted bases, rubber boots and helical springs.
- Ten vehicle families share rear-view mirror construction, including trucks, MRAPs, Humvees and technicals. Mirror glass uses its own reflective finish.
- Nine tank and artillery families share open gun tubes. Family-specific extractors, muzzle sensors and animation pivots remain authored separately; the T-55 retains its unsleeved barrel.
- Small attachments are most visible close up. Fixed fittings reuse the existing material batches. Each moving whip uses one pivot and one material batch, driven by one spring per vehicle; no physics bodies or mirror camera are added.

- Nearby visible antennas trail travel and react to acceleration and braking, then settle when stopped. Distant/hidden antennas skip motion updates.

Combined comparison of 19 representative vehicles; before is left and after is right within each pair.
Shared construction: antenna, mirror face and back, and hollow barrel.

videos.caption: Controlled motion comparison: rigid reference on the left, movement-responsive antenna on the right. Forward, lateral and reverse inputs are followed by settling.

entries.title: Better-built vehicle equipment
entries.summary: Shared vehicle equipment gains formed container shoulders, open chassis rails, forklift-ready pallets, winch housings and more convincing attachment hardware.
entries.body:
- Forty refinements improve twenty existing shared assemblies, including seats, storage, mirrors, armour skirts, aircraft gear, rocket pods and marine fittings. Most are close-up details rather than silhouette changes.
- Fuel cans support different body dimensions while keeping their caps, carrying bars and ribs together. Truck frames have open channel sections, and pallets have real gaps for lifting forks.
- Tempest ammunition loads use shared pallets with clearance beneath the folded crane. The tractor shares the hollow exhaust stack while retaining its silencer and rain cap.

screenshots.caption: Matched component close-ups: before on the left, after on the right. These shared builders supply the equipment on multiple vehicle designs.

entries.title: Round headlights with fitted optical detail
entries.summary: Round headlights now have a fitted rim, shallow reflector and ribbed lens detail across 19 vehicle families, while keeping their distinctive housings and guards.
entries.body:
- Extends from the Hunter to matching round lamps on trucks, light vehicles and armour, including their variants.
- Preserves protective cages, indicators and older vehicle details such as the T-55's missing infrared lens.
- Most visible up close. These are unlit lamps; this change does not add headlight beams. Wrecks lose the intact optical detail.

screenshots.caption: Hunter, Zamak and Qilin close-ups: before on the left, shared headlight detail on the right. Matched camera and lighting.

entries.title: Recessed grilles, open exhausts and sewn vehicle stowage
entries.summary: Military trucks gain deeper radiator grilles and hollow exhaust outlets. Shared rubber mudflaps and strapped canvas bags replace simple blocks across vehicle families.
entries.body:
- HEMTT, Tempest, Zamak and Hunter share radiator construction while retaining their own grille proportions and slat layout.
- HEMTT and Tempest exhausts have rolled rims, soot-lined interiors and lower heat shields.
- HEMTT, Tempest, Hunter, Ifrit and Strider mudflaps gain a curved lower edge, reinforcing ribs and mounting clamps.
- Padded stowage across NATO, CSAT and independent vehicles shares softened canvas shells, sewn welts, straps and buckles. Slammer and Scorcher storage supports become shallow trays so the bags are visible.
- The shared parts join existing material batches and keep their vehicle's animation pivots.

entries.title: Shared vehicle baskets, guards and equipment
entries.summary: Vehicle equipment gains open stowage baskets, toothed sprockets, fitted panels and shared construction for aircraft, truck and marine fittings.
entries.body:
Open baskets replace solid walls, radar arrays gain framed apertures, and equipment receives formed edges and attachment hardware. Twenty-two shared construction groups now supply compatible parts across multiple vehicle designs, so later improvements can reach them together.

The pass also moves more doors, windows, grilles, bins, steps, seats and exhausts onto existing shared builders. Specialized shapes retain their own construction; vehicle silhouettes and animation ownership are preserved.

screenshots.caption: Matched close-ups, before left and after right: Abrams basket and storage, Hunter bumper and light guards, Tigris radar and gun mounts. Small hardware is most visible up close.

entries.title: Shared vehicle equipment with more convincing construction
entries.summary: Fuel cans, ammo cans, shackles, smoke tubes, periscopes, hatches, tail lights, lifting eyes and rectangular headlights gain shared detail across the vehicles that use them.
entries.body:
- Fuel cans gain pressed ribs, filler caps and open handles. Sealed ammunition cans gain fitted lids, latches and handles that stay attached when rotated.
- Tow shackles and lifting eyes now have open holes, pins and mounting feet. Smoke tubes have hollow mouths while retaining each vehicle's bank layout.
- Periscopes gain sealed glass and protective lips; closed round hatches gain gaskets, hinge pins and open handles.
- Tail lights and rectangular headlights gain ribbed optical detail. Matching civilian round and fog lamps also use the shared round-headlight construction.
- Vehicle-specific silhouettes, guards, mounts and special equipment are retained. These details are most visible up close; lamps remain unlit, and wrecks lose intact optical surfaces.
